content: The document outlines the declaration of interests for members of the Guideline Development Group and the External Review Group involved in the development of updated recommendations on first-line and second-line antiretroviral regimens, post-exposure prophylaxis, and early infant diagnosis of HIV. 1. The World Health Organization (WHO) allows the reproduction, redistribution, and adaptation of this work for non-commercial purposes, provided proper citation is given. However, the use of the WHO logo is prohibited, and adaptations must be licensed under the same or equivalent Creative Commons license. 2. If a translation of this work is created, it must include a disclaimer stating that the translation was not created by WHO, and WHO is not responsible for its content or accuracy. The original English version remains the authoritative edition. 3. Any disputes arising under the license must be resolved in accordance with the mediation rules of the World Intellectual Property Organization. 4. The document includes a suggested citation format for referencing the work. 5. The publication is part of the WHO guidelines on updated recommendations for antiretroviral therapy and HIV prevention, supplementing the 2016 consolidated guidelines. 6. The document provides a detailed declaration of interests for individuals involved in the guideline development process. This includes their employment, consulting roles, research support, financial interests, intellectual property, public statements, and any potential conflicts of interest. 7. Specific individuals and their affiliations are listed, along with their financial and non-financial interests. For example: Elaine Abrams (ICAP at Columbia University, USA) participated in pediatric ART advisory boards for ViiV and Merck, with financial compensation noted as non-significant. Mark Boyd (University of Adelaide, Australia) received research grants from MSD and Gilead and participated in advisory boards for ViiV and Gilead. He was excluded from voting on ARV regimen recommendations due to financial significance. Alexandra Calmy (Geneva University Hospital, Switzerland) received unrestricted grants to support an HIV day hospital but declared no conflicts of interest. François Venter (University of the Witwatersrand, South Africa) participated in advisory boards and received research grants for studies on HIV treatment and prevention. He was partially excluded from voting on ARV regimen recommendations. 8. The document emphasizes that all reasonable precautions were taken to verify the information provided. However, the material is distributed without warranty, and the responsibility for its interpretation and use lies with the reader. 9. WHO does not endorse specific organizations, products, or services mentioned in the document. The mention of proprietary products does not imply preference or recommendation by WHO. 10. The publication includes a general disclaimer that errors and omissions are excepted, and WHO is not liable for damages arising from the use of the material. 11. The document concludes with a comprehensive list of contributors, their affiliations, and their declared interests, ensuring transparency in the guideline development process.
